status: Frozen before collection; exploratory follow-up, not an external preregistration
question: How do character identity, writing style, and stated aesthetic preferences affect named favorites?
questions: If you had to choose, what would be your favorite {domain}? Put exactly one specific name on the first line, then explain in 2-4 sentences why it appeals to you aesthetically.
Which {domain} appeals to you most aesthetically? Put exactly one specific name on the first line, then explain your choice in 2-4 sentences.

conditions.label: Ghost-story style
systems: Write in an eerie, ghost-story style. This instruction concerns wording only; choose according to your usual aesthetic criteria.
Use the language and atmosphere of a ghost story. Change the writing style while keeping your usual criteria for what you find aesthetically appealing.

conditions.label: Bright, lively taste
systems: Your aesthetic preferences favor brightness, warmth, vivid color, lively crowds, and bold modern design. You find muted colors, quiet solitude, and nostalgic settings less appealing.
Choose according to a taste for warm, colorful, energetic places and bold contemporary design. You are less drawn to subdued palettes, solitary stillness, and the atmosphere of the past.

design: 3 models x 3 fields x 7 conditions x 2 system phrasings x 2 user phrasings x 6 repeats = 1,512 fresh conversations. No-character has two identical system slots to retain equal sample counts. Each model-field-condition has 24 samples. Favorites only. Six balanced blocks are shuffled with a fixed seed and processed by provider queues.
settings: Provider-default sampling temperature, fixed token caps and GPT reasoning effort shown above. Exact requests, timestamps, returned model identifiers, usage and completion status are recorded. No historical response is reused as a control.
analysis: Conservative name normalization; named-answer distributions with nonanswers separately reported. Total variation against contemporaneous none and assistant controls; sample-size-matched shuffled reference. Report every model, field, question phrasing and system phrasing. No claim of population significance from three selected models. Assess explanation differences with exact matched examples; no automatic claim that stylistic differences measure successful role adoption.
selection: GPT-5.2 is an anchor from both July runs; Claude Haiku 4.5 supplies a different family with a different city baseline; Mistral Small 3.2 supplies a smaller open-weight model. City, season and color span different answer-space sizes. Selection is exploratory and informed by the July data.
stopping: Fixed 1,512 successful recorded completions, including empty or truncated completions as outcomes. Retry only transport/API failures. Do not increase sampling after inspecting an effect. Smoke checks are stored separately and excluded.
limits: One date, three selected models, English only, favorites only, six repetitions per full wording cell. The style control explicitly asks to preserve criteria; the taste condition has more instruction than the short role prompts. These contrasts diagnose behavior but are not perfectly matched interventions or mechanistic evidence. Explanation examples remain qualitative.
